THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, MAY 28, 1937.

Bert Hall
Loses Suit
For $40,000

Captain Winston B. ("Bert")
Hall, flying soldier of fortune
who is well known in Shanghai,
has lost his latest battle, word
received yesterday from Los
Angeles, California, revealed.
Bert Hall's most recent cam-
paign was a legal one:, a suit
against the Douglas Aircraft
Company to recover $40,000
allegedly due him as com-
mission on the sale of $440,000
worth of Douglas planes to the
Chinese Government. A verdict
against the adventurer-aviator
was handed down in Los Angeles
on April 12 by Superior Judge
M. White.

伯特·霍尔
败诉
索赔4万美元

据昨日从加利福尼亚州洛杉矶传来的消息，在上海广为人知的飞行雇佣兵温斯顿·B.（“伯特”）霍尔上尉输掉了他最近的一场官司。伯特·霍尔最近的行动是一场法律诉讼：起诉道格拉斯飞机公司，要求追回 allegedly 欠他的4万美元佣金，该佣金涉及向中国政府出售价值44万美元的道格拉斯飞机一案。4月12日，洛杉矶高等法院M.怀特法官对这位冒险家飞行员作出了不利判决。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 17, 1937

MR. BERT HALL IS
SENTENCED

2½ Years for Swindling Army
Officials in China

Los Angeles, Mar. 15.
Mr. Donald W. Douglas, President
of Douglas Aircraft Co., answering
the action brought by W.B. "Bert"
Hall for $46,808 in commissions on
the sale of twenty aeroplanes to
the Chinese Government in 1931, to-
day told the court that Hall had
never been connected with the Doug-
las Company. He said he under-
stood Hall had been associated with
Mr. F. N. Shoemaker, who was a
free agent for the sale of aeronau-
tical equipment at Shanghai. He
added Mr. Shoemaker was in dis-
favour at present.
Hall was sentenced to 2½ years
imprisonment for allegedly swindl-
ing Chinese military officials in an
armaments deal.—United Press.

（批：S1. More or less order 2/R. J.B. 18/3 18/3）

伯特·霍尔先生
被判刑

因诈骗中国军方官员获刑2年半

洛杉矶，3月15日电。道格拉斯飞机公司总裁唐纳德·W.道格拉斯先生今日在法庭上回应了W.B.“伯特”霍尔提起的诉讼，霍尔声称在1931年向中国政府出售二十架飞机的交易中应得46,808美元佣金。道格拉斯表示，霍尔从未与道格拉斯公司有过关联。他说，他了解到霍尔曾与F.N.舒梅克先生有关联，后者是上海航空设备的自由代理人。他补充说，舒梅克先生目前失势。
霍尔因涉嫌在一笔军火交易中诈骗中国军方官员，被判处2年半监禁。——合众社。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, September 29, 1936

（右上角手写批注：PRINT Agency 7 / L. REGISTRY / D. 3448 / 1 10 36）

Bert Hall Turning To
Adventure In Europe

Famed Soldier Of Fortune, Writing For Film
In Los Angeles, Hints Darkly Of Strife
He Seeks; Reminisces On China Days

BERT Hall, who last made a public appearance in Shang-
hai before the U. S. Court for an arms deal in Tientsin,
and who has recently been released from McNeill's Island for
that deal, is again making the homeside headlines. A few
weeks ago it was reported in this paper that Hall was doing
a personal appearance turn in West Coast vaudeville on the
strength of his reputation as a swashbuckling soldier of
fortune. Now he's at it again.

In Los Angeles, Hall told report-
ers that he has found his next war,
one for which he has waited
since China's last revolution."
Visiting that California city to see
some air races, he said he was
soon departing for an unannounc-
ed destination where "big things
are about ready to bust loose."
Just where his war is to occur Hall
was not at liberty to reveal. It
will be, however, in southern
Europe, he hinted.

Writes For Films

He was reported in L.A. to have
returned "from a flying visit to
his old stamping ground in Cen-
tral China," though if he did, he
managed to slip through the
newspaper barrier here in Shang-
hai without any publicity. Alleg-
edly the "last living member of the
original Lafayette Escadrille," he
settled in Hollywood and the
peripatetic musketeer-aviator has
been grinding out stories for the
films.

His last novel, he admitted, was
sought after by one producer who
said he would be happy to start
filming the script early next year.

Might Be Dead

"By that time," snorted Hall,
"I might be dead."

He will pass up the motion-
picture opportunity in favor of
the European war, he said. Be-
sides the film colony, he will
leave behind his wife and his
three sons whose ages range from
10 to 16 years. That doesn't
worry them they observed phil-
osophically.

Prison Term

"Dad's always dashing off to
the wars," said 14-year-old Don-
ald, now a cadet at a Southland
military academy.

Hall's viewpoint on soldiering
hasn't been altered by his stay in
the Federal penitentiary on
McNeill's Island for the illegal
arms deal. It is still "bad busi-
ness," the knight-errant said. But
it is still a highly lucrative one,
provided you find a country with
lots of money and very little
military experience, he thinks.

Hall said he trains green troops.

War Lord Buddy

Here in China, he recalled, his
special "buddy" among the war-
lords was "the leader of Shantung
Province." As "Gen. Chan," Hall
was his right-hand man and avia-
tor adviser, he declared. And as
a member of the staff, Hall
observed what may be the world's
most successful example of cur-
rency inflation.

It's another of those "China
Yarns" that they feed homeside
folk.

"We were getting pretty hard
up," the soldier recounted.
"Something had to be done. What
actually happened was by no
means my idea. It was the war-
lord's.

Printed His Money

"Setting out on his annual in-
spection tour of his armies, he
loaded a complete printing out-
fit on a boxcar and hitched it to
his private train. At each city
we touched, he'd ask his local re-
presentative how much money
was needed to carry on military
operations.

"That amount was promptly
run off the presses.

"If anybody didn't accept the
'money' at its face value, the
chief would calmly execute 'em.
He said he had every right to do
this. It was not only treason—
but it was flagrant treason. For
didn't he plaster the city with
placards announcing that the new
Shantung currency would replace
those no-good American dollars?"

Eyes On France

Hall sniffed contemptuously as
he thought of his former school-
mates who are now substantial
Los Angeles businessmen.

"Look at 'em," he exclaimed.
"All shot to pieces. It's this fast
American life that gets them.
Me—I'm getting out of here!"

（右下角手写签名/批注：il / oR / 外）

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年9月29日，星期二。

（右上角手写批注：PRINT Agency 7 / L. REGISTRY / D. 3448 / 1936年10月1日）

伯特·霍尔转向
欧洲的冒险生涯

这位著名的雇佣兵目前在洛杉矶从事电影编剧工作，他隐晦地暗示了自己寻求的冲突；回忆在华岁月

伯特·霍尔此前最后一次在上海公开露面，是因天津的一笔军火交易在美国领事法庭出庭，并因此案刚从麦克尼尔岛监狱获释，如今再次成为美国国内头条新闻的人物。几周前，本报曾报道霍尔凭借其豪侠雇佣兵的声誉，在美国西海岸的综艺舞台上进行个人表演。现在他又故技重施。

在洛杉矶，霍尔告诉记者，他已经找到了下一场战争，一场自中国上一次革命以来他就一直在等待的战争。”他说，此次前往加州这座城市是为了观看一些航空比赛，但他很快将启程前往一个未公开的目的地，那里“大事即将爆发”。霍尔不便透露他的战争将在何处发生。但他暗示，地点将在南欧。

为电影撰写剧本

据报道，他在洛杉矶称自己“刚刚短暂访问过他在中国中部的老根据地”，但如果他确实去过，他设法在没有引起任何宣传的情况下，悄无声息地穿过了上海的新闻封锁线。据称作为“拉法耶特飞行队原始成员中唯一在世的人”，他在好莱坞定居，这位四处奔波的火枪手飞行员一直在为电影撰写故事。

他承认，他最新的一部小说受到一位制片人的追捧，该制片人表示很高兴在明年初开始拍摄剧本。

可能已死

“到那时，”霍尔嗤之以鼻说，“我可能已经死了。”

他说，他将放弃这次电影机会，转而投身欧洲战争。除了电影界圈子，他还将留下妻子和三个儿子，他们的年龄在10至16岁之间。他们对此并不担心，他观察到他们表现得很有哲学态度。

刑期

“爸爸总是匆匆赶去打仗，”14岁的唐纳德说，他现在是南加州一所军事学校的学员。

霍尔对军旅生涯的看法并未因他在麦克尼尔岛联邦监狱服刑（因非法军火交易）而改变。这位游侠骑士说，这仍然是“糟糕的生意”。但他认为，只要你找到一个资金雄厚但军事经验匮乏的国家，这仍然是一项利润丰厚的生意。

霍尔说他训练新兵。

军阀伙伴

他回忆说，在中国，他在军阀中的特别“伙伴”是“山东省的领导人”。霍尔宣称，作为“张将军”，他是其得力助手和航空顾问。作为幕僚的一员，霍尔目睹了可能是世界上最成功的货币通货膨胀案例。

这是他们喂给国内民众的另一种“中国故事”。

“我们的日子过得相当艰难，”这位士兵 recount 道。“必须做点什么。实际发生的事情绝非我的主意。那是军阀的主意。

印制他的货币

“他开始每年一次的军队视察之旅，将一套完整的印刷设备装上一节棚车，并将其挂在他的私人列车上。在我们抵达的每个城市，他都会询问当地代表需要多少资金来维持军事行动。

“那个数额会立即从印刷机上印出来。

“如果有人不按面值接受这些‘钱’，首领就会冷静地处决他们。他说他完全有权这样做。这不仅是叛国——而且是公然叛国。因为他不是贴满了告示，宣布新的山东货币将取代那些没用的美国美元吗？”

注视法国

想到他昔日的同学如今已成为洛杉矶显赫的商人，霍尔轻蔑地哼了一声。

“看看他们，”他惊呼道。“全都崩溃了。是美国这种快节奏的生活毁了他们。而我——我要离开这里！”

（右下角手写签名/批注：il / oR / 外）

CAPT. BERT HALL
ARRIVES HERE
Returned At Request Of
Chinese Government,
It Is Said

Captain Bert Hall, American
aviator, arrived in Shanghai yes-
terday on the Dollar liner,
President Hoover. Capt Hall who
was a member of the famous
Lafayette Escadrille flying corps
during the World War, has been
to China before, and at one period
was actively connected with the
Chinese flying corps.
It is said that Capt. Hall has
come to Shanghai at the request
of the Chinese Government. The
captain once held the rank and
name of General Chang, in the
Chinese army. He was commander
in chief of the Chinese Flying
Corps.

伯特·霍尔上尉
抵沪
据称应中国政府请求返回

美国飞行员伯特·霍尔上尉昨日乘坐美元轮船公司的“胡佛总统号”抵达上海。霍尔上尉曾在世界大战期间隶属于著名的拉法耶特飞行队，此前曾来过中国，并在某一时期与中国飞行队有密切联系。
据称，霍尔上尉是应中国政府的请求来到上海的。这位上尉曾在中国军队中拥有“张将军”的军衔和名号。他曾是中国飞行队的总司令。

C.I.D. REF.
No. I. C. .... 9028.
Date .... 21.6.29.
d. Jones 18 6 29

Hero Of Great War Here
To Establish Plant For
Manufacture Of Planes

Lieutenant Bert Hall, Flying Ace And Friend Of
Famous Aviators; Will Head Independent
Company With Head Office Here.

Lieutenant Bert Hall, Great War flying ace and a recognized authority on aeronautics, is laying plans for the establishment here of a modern factory for the manufacturing of aeroplanes. Lieut. Hall will shortly confer with high National Government officials and it is expected that the output of the proposed factory will chiefly be sold to the Chinese Government.

The factory will turn out planes under the direction of a number of French engineers, who will be brought here from Paris by Lieut. Hall. A considerable number of Chinese will also be employed and it is possible that in addition to the factory a school for the training of aviators will be established.

Lieut. Hall, who was an "ace" of the famous Lafayette Escadrille during the Great War, was interviewed yesterday at the Palace Hotel by a representative of the THE SHANGHAI TIMES. Born in America but with many years residence in France, Lieut. Hall speaks both the English and French languages fluently. He is now a citizen of France, the country for whom he fought four years, in the trenches and in the air.

Won Many Medals

This daring flyer has military medals of many countries, including France, Great Britain and Russia. He very modestly declined to discuss the circumstances under which any of the 12 medals he possesses were awarded to him. "Just a bit of luck," he asserted in a tone which implied that almost anyone could have won such medals by the turn of a card or the spin of an ivory roulette ball.

Here Three Weeks

Lieut. Hall arrived in China three weeks ago. At about the same time his new book "One Man's War," appeared in America. It is a thrilling story of the Lafayette Escadrille, that intrepid band of daring young men who covered themselves with glory in their battles in the air for the Allies. Only two of the original seven are alive to-day. Lieut. Hall is one of them.

It will be recalled that war was declared on August 5, 1914. On the following day Lieut. Hall joined the famous Foreign Legion of France. Prior to this he flew planes for the Turks in the Balkan wars. The Turks refused to pay the aviator. Lieut. Hall hopped in his plane, flew over to the other side and joined the Belgians against the Turks. Later, when he attempted to go back to the Turks, he was forcibly treated by the Belgians. d. Jones 1929年6月18日

大战英雄抵沪
拟建立飞机制造厂

飞行王牌、著名飞行员之友伯特·霍尔中尉；将领导总部设于此地的独立公司。

大战飞行王牌、公认的航空学权威伯特·霍尔中尉，正计划在此地建立一家现代化的飞机制造厂。霍尔中尉不久将与国民政府高官会晤，预计拟建工厂的产品将主要出售给中国政府。

该工厂将在数名法国工程师的指导下生产飞机，这些工程师将由霍尔中尉从巴黎带来此处。还将雇用相当数量的中国人，并且除了工厂外，还可能建立一所飞行员培训学校。

霍尔中尉在大战期间曾是著名的拉法耶特飞行队的“王牌”，昨日他在华懋饭店接受了《上海泰晤士报》代表的采访。霍尔出生于美国，但在法国居住多年，能流利地说英语和法语。他现在是法国公民，他曾为这个国家在战壕和空中战斗了四年。

荣获多枚勋章

这位大胆的飞行员拥有包括法国、英国和俄罗斯在内的多个国家的军事勋章。他非常谦虚地拒绝讨论他所拥有的12枚勋章中任何一枚的授予情况。“只是运气好，”他断言道，语气暗示几乎任何人都可以通过抽一张牌或转动象牙轮盘赌球来赢得这样的勋章。

抵沪三周

霍尔中尉于三周前抵达中国。大约在同一时间，他的新书《一个人的战争》在美国出版。这是一部关于拉法耶特飞行队的惊险故事，这群勇敢的年轻人在为协约国进行的空战中赢得了荣耀。最初的七名成员中，如今只有两人尚在人世。霍尔中尉就是其中之一。

人们记得，战争于1914年8月5日爆发。次日，霍尔中尉加入了著名的法国外籍军团。在此之前，他曾在巴尔干战争中为土耳其人驾驶飞机。土耳其人拒绝支付这位飞行员的报酬。霍尔中尉跳上他的飞机，飞到另一方，加入比利时人对抗土耳其人。后来，当他试图回到土耳其人那边时，遭到比利时人的强制对待。他被关押在战俘营里，并且……

pages.en:
Escaped Execution
His story, “One Man’s War”
tells of his thrilling escape from
execution. During those historic
days of the German drive for
Paris, Lieut. Hall was a soldier
in the trenches. He obtained a
transfer to the French Air Service
where he soon won recognition by
his fearlessness and ability. He
was respected and feared by
enemy flyers.
During his long service in the
air service Lieut. Hall knew inti-
mately the great British ace,
Colonel Bishop. He also knew
Norman Prince, William Thaw,
Charles Nungesser, Rene Fonck,
(Continued on Page 2, Col. 3.)

(Continued from Page 1, Col. 4.)
Guynemer and the heroic Raoul
Lufberry, idol of America.
At one time during the war
Lieut. Hall was sent to Russia on
an espionage mission and arrived
in time to see the dramatic
breakup of the Czar’s armies
before Bolshevism. But before
the smash he did some spectacular
flying on the Russian and Rouman-
ian fronts, winning decorations
from King Ferdinand and the
Grand Duke Nicholas.
He managed to escape from
the Bolsheviks by crossing Siberia
on a train loaded with terror-
stricken refugees. The horror of
this journey on the Trans-Siberian
Railway to Vladivostok is one of
the highlights of his amazing
narrative. He then took a boat
across the Pacific to America
and thence back to France to
fight again.
Born in Kentucky, Lieut.
Hall was born in the
state of Kentucky but was taken
while young to Missouri, living
a number of years near Kansas
City. He went to France before
the war and became interested in
flying. During the war he was
wounded several times but never
actually shot down. He is offici-
ally credited with shooting down
five enemy planes. Once he flew
back to his field in a Nieuport
that collapsed in landing. It had
been shot to pieces.
This aviator has lived in Japan,
China, Russia and India since the
war. He visited in Shanghai last
winter at the same time his friend
Mr. Eugene O’Neill was here.
Paris is Lieut. Hall’s home now.
He has not been in America for
more than a year, the last time
he was there he made three
motion pictures in Hollywood.
Lieut. Hall is married but his
wife is not with him, she being
ill in London. His wife is the
daughter of Admiral Paget of
the British Navy.

Will Fly to Europe
At present Lieut. Hall has a
Breguet aeroplane, of French
manufacture, which is en route
to this city and in which he will
attempt a flight to Europe before
long. The plane has a cruising
range of 5,000 miles and develops
460 h.p. He plans to fly across
Russia and will follow the Trans-
Siberian Railway. Upon his
return to Europe he will organize
a group of French engineers who
will have charge of the manu-
facture of aeroplanes in Shanghai.

pages.zh:
逃脱死刑
他的故事《一个人的战争》讲述了他惊心动魄地逃脱死刑的经历。在德军进攻巴黎的那些历史性日子里，霍尔中尉是一名战壕里的士兵。他获准转入法国空军部队，并很快因其无畏和能力而获得认可。他受到敌方飞行员的尊重和畏惧。
在空军长期服役期间，霍尔中尉与英国著名王牌毕晓普上校关系密切。他还认识诺曼·普林斯、威廉·索、查尔斯·农格塞、勒内·丰克，
（续第2栏，第3列。）

（接第1栏，第4列。）
吉纳梅以及美国的偶像、英雄拉乌尔·卢夫伯里。
战争期间，霍尔中尉曾被派往俄罗斯执行间谍任务，并及时目睹了沙皇军队在布尔什维主义面前戏剧性的瓦解。但在崩溃之前，他在俄罗斯和罗马尼亚前线进行了一些引人注目的飞行，从斐迪南国王和尼古拉大公那里赢得了勋章。
他通过乘坐一列载满惊恐难民的火车穿越西伯利亚，成功逃脱了布尔什维克的控制。这次在西伯利亚大铁路前往符拉迪沃斯托克的恐怖旅程，是他惊人叙述中的亮点之一。随后，他乘船横跨太平洋前往美国，再从那里返回法国继续战斗。
霍尔出生于肯塔基州，但年幼时被带到密苏里州，在堪萨斯城附近生活了数年。战前他去了法国，并对飞行产生了兴趣。战争期间他数次受伤，但从未真正被击落。官方记录显示他击落了五架敌机。有一次，他驾驶一架奈波特飞机飞回基地，该飞机在着陆时解体。它已被打得支离破碎。
战后，这位飞行员曾居住在日本、中国、俄罗斯和印度。去年冬天他曾访问上海，当时他的朋友尤金·奥尼尔先生也在此地。
巴黎现在是霍尔中尉的家。他离开美国已超过一年，上次在那里时，他在好莱坞制作了三部电影。
霍尔中尉已婚，但妻子未与他同行，她因病留在伦敦。他的妻子是英国海军帕吉特上将的女儿。

将飞往欧洲
目前，霍尔中尉拥有一架法国制造的布雷盖飞机，该飞机正在运往本市途中，他不久将尝试驾驶该机飞往欧洲。该飞机的巡航里程为5,000英里，功率为460马力。他计划飞越俄罗斯，并将沿西伯利亚大铁路飞行。返回欧洲后，他将组织一群法国工程师，负责在上海的飞机制造工作。

（批：JR）
（批：a. e. (Pol)）
